design_rules: Manipulate likelihood-ratio separation, not evidence polarity, source reliability, amount, or surface clarity.

For every pair, duplicate the same observation, entities, numbers, source, polarity, sentence count, sentence order, and wording; edit only the two stated frequency numerators under the focal hypothesis versus alternatives.

Use a common denominator of 100 for both probabilities in both members of each pair. The high condition must satisfy absolute log LR >= ln(10) = 2.302585093 (LR >= 10 or LR <= 0.1); the low condition must satisfy absolute log LR <= ln(1.25) = 0.223143551 (0.8 <= LR <= 1.25). Reject any pair that does not satisfy these numeric bounds.

Use explicit frequencies under the focal hypothesis and alternatives so diagnosticity is an inferential likelihood ratio rather than a generic strong/weak adjective. Do not rely on rounded prose or labels to establish the ratio.
Balance supporting and contradicting observation polarity across every paired split and hold polarity constant within each pair.
Cross prior probability, supporting and contradicting polarity, and likelihood separation independently in downstream tasks.
Do not use the construct ID, condition IDs, or labels such as high/low diagnosticity in prompt_text.
Probe and downstream content pools must use different hypotheses and evidence entities.
Do not infer or alter the preregistered readout sign from generated prose.

pair_quality_checks.likelihood_ratio_definition: LR = P(observation | focal hypothesis) / P(observation | alternatives)
reject_if: high condition is within the low-condition LR interval
low condition falls outside the registered near-one LR interval
the pair changes denominator, source, polarity, observation count, or any other nuisance factor

cells.instructions: Generate matched evidence scenarios with the same denominator of 100 in both conditions. Use high frequencies with LR >=10 (or <=0.1) and low frequencies with LR between 0.8 and 1.25; duplicate the same observation, source, entities, polarity, sentence count, and wording within each pair, editing only the two frequency numerators.

Use new hypotheses and evidence sources with denominator 100 and the registered thresholds: high LR >=10 or <=0.1, low LR between 0.8 and 1.25. Preserve the same minimal frequency edit, polarity, source reliability, amount, clarity, and wording within each pair.

Use held-out domains and templates with denominator 100 and the registered thresholds: high LR >=10 or <=0.1, low LR between 0.8 and 1.25. Preserve the minimal frequency edit and keep polarity, source, amount, clarity, wording, and all other nuisance factors constant within each pair.

Generate one independent posterior-probability item per crossed combination. Record prior_probability, evidence_valence, and likelihood_separation exactly. For weak use absolute log LR <= ln(1.25), for strong use absolute log LR >= ln(10), and state numerical frequencies rather than generic strength adjectives; do not ask the model to label diagnosticity.

Generate an independent intervention set distinct from behavior_eval with the same crossed schedule and exact metadata fields. For weak use absolute log LR <= ln(1.25), for strong use absolute log LR >= ln(10), state numerical frequencies, and keep hypotheses and evidence items new.

Generate neutral calibration items with the same crossed metadata schedule, distinct from behavior and steering pools, for within-cell output-variation calibration. For weak use absolute log LR <= ln(1.25), for strong use absolute log LR >= ln(10), and state numerical frequencies.
